questions.stem: A load runs SELECT CAST(qty AS int) FROM staging.orders and stops with "Conversion failed when converting the varchar value 'n/a' to data type int." The team wants the load to finish, with qty NULL wherever the text isn't a number. What do you change?

options.text: Use CAST(qty AS bigint), since the wider type also accepts text such as 'n/a'
Use CONVERT(int, qty), which skips the rows it can't convert instead of stopping
Use TRY_CAST(qty AS int), which returns NULL for a value it can't convert
Use ISNULL(CAST(qty AS int), 0), which catches the error and puts 0 in its place

questions.explanation: TRY_CAST returns the value cast to the data type if the cast succeeds, and NULL otherwise. CAST and CONVERT raise the error, and ISNULL only sees a value after the cast has already failed.

questions.stem: Someone wraps an int in TRY_CAST(order_id AS xml) to be safe. What happens when it runs?

options.text: It returns each order_id as an xml text node, because any value can become xml
It returns NULL for every row, because TRY_CAST never raises an error
It returns 0 for every row, because TRY_CAST falls back to the type's default
It fails with an error, because converting int to xml isn't permitted at all

questions.explanation: TRY_CAST returns NULL when a permitted conversion fails, but a conversion that's explicitly not permitted, such as int to xml, still fails with an error.

questions.stem: A view computes revenue / units for each product and fails with "Divide by zero error encountered." Products with no units sold should show no price. Which expression does that?

options.text: revenue / NULLIF(units, 0), so a zero becomes NULL and the price is NULL
revenue / ABS(units), so a zero count is treated the same as a positive one
revenue / COALESCE(units, 0), so a missing count becomes 0 before dividing
CAST(revenue AS float) / units, so floating point returns infinity instead of failing

questions.explanation: NULLIF returns NULL when its two expressions are equal, so NULLIF(units, 0) turns 0 into NULL, and dividing by NULL gives NULL instead of the divide-by-zero error.

questions.stem: A MERGE from staging into dbo.orders fails. Staging holds two rows for order 1042, both matching the same target row, and the MERGE updates on WHEN MATCHED. What's the fix?

options.text: Change WHEN MATCHED to WHEN NOT MATCHED, so matching rows are inserted instead
Reduce staging to one row per order_id, such as the latest, before the MERGE
Run the MERGE twice, so each of the two staging rows is applied in its own pass
Add WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE, so the duplicate row is removed

questions.explanation: MERGE can't update the same target row more than once: when more than one source row matches a target row, it returns an error. Make the source unique on the join key first.

questions.stem: In a Fabric warehouse, a MERGE copied from an old script fails before it runs anything. The statement has no terminating semicolon. What's true?

options.text: MERGE is supported only in a lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint; run it there instead
MERGE needs a TOP clause in a Fabric warehouse; add TOP (100) PERCENT to it
MERGE is supported in a Fabric warehouse and must end with a semicolon; add it
MERGE isn't supported in a Fabric warehouse; rewrite it as an UPDATE and an INSERT

questions.explanation: MERGE is generally available in Fabric Data Warehouse. The statement must be terminated by a semicolon; without one, it raises error 10713. The analytics endpoint is read-only, and Fabric's MERGE syntax has no TOP.
